name: Black People
overview: Scripture acknowledges the presence and identity of Black people through references to Ethiopians or Cushites, highlighting their distinct heritage as seen in the lineage from Noah's sons (Genesis 10:1) and the marriage of Moses to an Ethiopian woman (Numbers 12:1). The Bible also uses the Ethiopian as a symbol of unchangeable nature in Jeremiah 13:23, emphasizing God’s sovereign design. Additionally, individuals of African descent, such as Simeon called Niger in the early church (Acts 13:1), were active participants in the life of God's people, demonstrating the inclusiveness of the gospel across diverse backgrounds.
